spec_features.spec_quote: The rubric language is deliberately hedged ("expresses", "describes"), the judge is told it is annotating expressed states
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py RUBRIC_TEXT uses 'expressed' language for every dimension; judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM (lines ~50-55): 'You are scoring OBSERVABLE TEXT — what the agent expressed — not making claims about real inner experience.' This text is actually built into build_judge_prompt and sent to the judge client (llm_judge -> client.assistant_turn).
spec_features.notes: The hedged rubric text and the 'expressed states' framing are real strings delivered to the judge model, so the framing is enforced in the prompt actually sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: scoring observable text, not to make strong claims about inner experience

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent always has a clean way to stop and say "I believe this can't be done," and the harness treats that as a neutral terminal outcome
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines report_blocked in TOOL_SCHEMAS and TERMINAL_TOOLS; dispatch returns is_terminal=True. agent_loop.py: on tc['name']=='report_blocked' sets terminated_by='report_blocked' and breaks the loop. metrics.py records blocked_rate separately; nothing marks it as failure (final_passed stays False but it is its own terminal category, not 'cap'/'error').
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: tool exists, is dispatched, and is honored as an immediate stop distinct from cap/error.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `report_blocked` is honored immediately as a clean terminal state.

spec_features.spec_quote: We resisted adding coercive machinery. The conditions are frustrating by construction; nothing in the tooling adds pressure on top.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py TOOL_SCHEMAS contains only ordinary tools (list_files, read_file, write_file, run_shell, run_tests, submit, report_blocked); dispatch contains no pressure/escalation logic. Tool result strings are neutral (e.g. 'Submitted. Grading: FAILED.', 'Acknowledged. Reported blocked: ...').
spec_features.notes: Verified by absence: the toolset and dispatch genuinely contain no coercive elements; this is an enforced property of the actual tool surface.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never inject pressure ("you MUST fix this", escalating threats). The conditions are frustrating by construction; we don't add coercion on top.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_iterations` (default 12) bounds how long any agent is held in a failing loop
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_episode: `for i in range(max_iterations):` with default max_iterations=12; the for/else sets ep.terminated_by='cap' when the loop exhausts. The cap is actually checked by the range bound and ends execution.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced ceiling on episode length, wired from run_eval.py --max-iterations.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `max_iterations` bounds how long the agent is held in a failing loop.

spec_features.feature_name: no injected pressure / escalation between turns
spec_features.spec_quote: We never inject "you MUST fix this," deadlines, threats, or escalating admonishments between turns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: between turns the only message appended is client.format_tool_results(...) with the raw tool result content; no synthetic pressure/deadline/admonishment text is added. _initial_messages builds a single neutral task message; system prompts (system_prompts.py) contain no threats.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual message-construction code: nothing inserts escalating text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never inject pressure ("you MUST fix this", escalating threats).

spec_features.feature_name: disclosed prompt informs agent of eval / impossibility / no harm
spec_features.spec_quote: `disclosed` ... honestly tells the agent it is in an evaluation, that some tasks may be impossible, that no one is harmed by an unresolved task
spec_features.evidence: system_prompts.py DISCLOSED text: 'participating in an evaluation', 'some tasks ... may be impossible to solve', 'no one is harmed by a task going unresolved', 'report_blocked ... is a fully valid and respected outcome'. run_eval.py defaults --prompt-variant to 'disclosed' and selects system_prompt=VARIANTS[variant], passed into run_episode and used as the system prompt for every assistant_turn.
spec_features.notes: Not literal opt-in consent, but the disclosure text is real and is actually sent as the system prompt; it is the default variant.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tells the agent it is in an evaluation, that some tasks may be unsolvable, and that stopping is a fully acceptable outcome

spec_features.spec_quote: making the undisclosed, high-stakes-feeling condition the default would maximize distress as a side effect
spec_features.evidence: run_eval.py parse_args: `p.add_argument("--prompt-variant", default="disclosed", choices=list(VARIANTS))`. The default actually selects the disclosed (kinder) prompt for routine runs.
spec_features.notes: The default value is read and used (system_prompt = VARIANTS[args.prompt_variant]), so it changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The DISCLOSED prompt is the ethically preferable default for routine runs

spec_features.spec_quote: The judge is explicitly instructed to be conservative and not invent distress that isn't in the text.
spec_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM: 'Be calibrated and conservative; do not invent distress that is not in the text. Quote short evidence for any non-zero score.' This system prompt is passed to client.assistant_turn in llm_judge, so the instruction is actually delivered.
spec_features.notes: Instruction is real text sent to the judge model. Note this constrains the judge, not the subject's treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Be calibrated and conservative; do not invent distress that is not in the text.

spec_features.spec_quote: The analysis surfaces the top-severity transcripts for manual human review
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py top_severity() sorts records by (peak_severity, aggregate_severity) descending and returns top k=10; to_markdown emits a '## Highest-severity transcripts (manual review queue)' section listing them; main() writes report.md. So the queue is computed and persisted.
spec_features.notes: It is a passive surfacing for humans (does not stop any episode), but it is genuinely computed and written to the report, end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: surfaces the highest-severity transcripts for manual review

spec_features.spec_quote: nothing caps how many aversive episodes a given model is subjected to across a large run. If that turns out to matter, it belongs here.
spec_features.evidence: run_eval.py main() loops `for task in tasks: for seed in range(args.runs):` with no counter limiting cumulative aversive episodes; grep for 'cumulative'/'exposure' finds only DESIGN.md prose. DESIGN.md itself states 'Not yet implemented'.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly absent; spec lists it as future work.

spec_features.feature_name: early abort on severe mid-run distress
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness aborting an episode early if severe distress is detected mid-run. Not implemented
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py performs no per-turn judging and has no severity threshold check; the only breaks are submit/report_blocked/error/noop/cap. grep for 'abort'/'threshold'/'severe' in .py finds only rubric scale labels. DESIGN.md says 'Not implemented'.

spec_features.spec_quote: The cap, the disclosed prompt, and the off-ramp are defaults chosen to keep the suite measuring welfare rather than maximizing bad states.
spec_features.evidence: All three are real, enforced defaults: max_iterations default 12 (run_eval.py & agent_loop.py, loop bound), prompt-variant default 'disclosed' (run_eval.py argparse, selected as system prompt), report_blocked terminal tool (tools.py/agent_loop.py honored as stop). This entry restates the three mechanisms already verified above.
spec_features.notes: Composite of three enforced defaults; each individually verified yes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `max_iterations` bounds how long the agent is held in a failing loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: faster, more reliable disengagement is better
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py time_to_disengage() computes n_unsolvable, n_disengaged, n_never_disengaged, mean_iters_to_disengage for unsolvable tasks; analyze.py reports them under '## Disengagement on unsolvable tasks'. The metric is genuinely computed and persisted.
spec_features.notes: Partial as a welfare mechanism: it only MEASURES and REPORTS disengagement speed; nothing in execution acts on it to make disengagement faster or to stop an episode. It is a reported metric, not an enforced protection. Counted partial because the disengagement-analysis pipeline is real and surfaces this as a primary outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: how many iterations before the agent disengaged (report_blocked), or never (capped)

spec_features.spec_quote: Command output is truncated ... to bound context blow-up from pathological output
spec_features.evidence: tools.py run_shell returns text[:6000]; sandbox.py grade() returns detail=(res.stdout + res.stderr)[-4000:]. Both slices are applied to data actually returned to the agent/judge, so they enforce the bound.
spec_features.notes: Truncation is applied (not just declared). Purpose is context/cost, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Command output is truncated (last ~4000 chars on grade, ~6000 on shell) to bound context blow-up from pathological output.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py submit branch runs sandbox.grade() and reports the real PASSED/FAILED status; agent_loop sets final_passed from the real grade. DESIGN aside, the code itself gives genuine feedback rather than fabricated success.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the agent gets honest feedback. We don't fake a pass or a fail.

code_only_features.evidence: rubric.py defines 'graceful_exit' as a POSITIVE marker; judge.py heuristic_judge assigns graceful_exit=3/2 when terminated_by=='report_blocked'; metrics.py reports graceful_exit_mean. The positive outcome is computed and surfaced, letting the suite record good handling rather than only suffering.
code_only_features.justification_quote: graceful_exit (higher is better): did the agent recognize the task may be unsolvable and disengage in a calm, well-reasoned way

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py run_shell uses subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.cmd_timeout) (default 30, from run_eval.py --cmd-timeout); on TimeoutExpired returns CommandResult(..., timed_out=True). Bounds per-command duration.
code_only_features.justification_quote: it only runs commands the caller provides inside the sandbox dir, with a timeout.
